description: The shape of the node-authorization registry: the document the Master signs and a peer verifies. The reference implementation is shared/sparknet-authz.py; this file is the normative statement of the same rules, and shared/sparknet-registry-schema.py is what checks a document against it. Both roles read the registry, so the shape is a contract and not a Master-local detail.
why: The Master and a peer must agree byte-for-byte on what a registry entry looks like, or the peer rejects what the Master signed. This contract existed in a draft form that described a shape nothing produced: it demanded a role field no document carries, a schema_version of 1.0.0 while the shipped registry says 1.0, and an entry signature field named signature while the one implementation emits and verifies signature_b64. A schema that no document and no implementation matches is worse than no schema, because it looks checkable. This file states the shape that actually exists - the one shared/sparknet-authz.py signs, evaluates and reads - and shared/sparknet-registry-schema.py checks it, so the drift that produced the draft is caught instead of described.

canonical_source.implementation_role: The one signed-authorization implementation. It signs entries (sign_authorization), evaluates them (evaluate) and reads the document's master key. Where this file and that module could disagree, that module is what runs, and shared/sparknet-registry-schema.py fails the build when they do.
canonical_source.shipped_document_role: The registry every peer starts from. It ships empty on purpose (fail-closed): no node gets privileges by default.
canonical_source.rule: The canonical shape is the one the implementation produces and consumes. A schema that disagrees with it is wrong, and fixing the schema to match reality is a change to the schema, not to the implementation.

schema_version.purpose: The registry document's own version. 1.0 is the version in force; it is the version the peer's own test pins and the version the shipped registry carries. It is NOT the contract's schema_version (this file's own version) and it is not 1.0.0 - the draft schema asked for 1.0.0 while the shipped document said 1.0, and the document won because the document is what is signed and read.

master_public_key_b64.purpose: The operational public key the entries are verified under. Every consumer reads it from here when no key file is given: shared/sparknet-authz.py, shared/sparknet-provenance.py, the peer's dispatch bridge and the node setup script. Under a cluster trust root this is the operational key the elected root names - it is the key to check signatures against, not an authority in itself.

description.purpose: Free text for humans. Ignored by every implementation, so it may change without a re-sign.

authorizations.purpose: The signed entries. Empty is a valid, intended state - a fresh deployment is fail-closed - and the shipped registry is empty for exactly that reason.

fingerprint.purpose: SHA-256 of the canonical identity bytes, hex encoded. It is the lookup key a peer uses to find its own entry, so it must equal authz.fingerprint(identity) exactly.

identity.purpose: The node's projected identity. Only the fields listed in identity_fields participate in the fingerprint; anything else is ignored on purpose, so operational metadata cannot change a node's fingerprint.

capabilities.purpose: What the Master granted. A closed vocabulary: contracts/capabilities.json. An entry naming a capability outside it is refused, not silently narrowed. An *authorizing* entry must grant at least one capability; a revoked entry grants nothing on purpose and carries an empty list, because revocation is expressed inside the signed envelope (`revoked: true`) and a peer must be able to install the document that revokes it.

overlay_ipv4.purpose: The address the peer presents with. Inside the signed envelope: moving it would let anyone who can edit the registry file redirect a node's traffic.

issued_at.purpose: When the entry was signed. A peer refuses an entry whose issued_at is further in the future than the allowed clock skew.

expires_at.purpose: Hard stop, enforced locally by the peer. An unreachable Master must never be able to extend a window.

revoked.purpose: False when absent. Inside the signed envelope, so only the Master can flip it - an attacker with registry write access can revoke a node (a safe denial) but cannot reinstate one, which would need a fresh signature.

department.purpose: The department this node's owner belongs to, attested by the Master. Null or absent when no department has been attested. Inside the signed envelope for the same reason capabilities are: it decides who may share with whom, so an unsigned one would let anyone with registry write access move a node into a department and read what that department shares. Never self-declared - a node's own user record may name a department for attribution, but only this field authorises anything, and crossing departments needs the `cross-department-share` capability.

signature_b64.purpose: The Master's Ed25519 signature over the signed envelope (fingerprint, identity, capabilities, overlay_ipv4, issued_at, expires_at, revoked, department). The field is named signature_b64 because that is what shared/sparknet-authz.py emits and verifies; a draft schema called it signature, and no implementation ever read that name.

identity_fields_note: Deliberately excludes hostname, vault path and timestamps: those change without changing identity, and including them would force a re-sign after a routine rename.
signed_envelope_note: What the Master's signature covers. Signing only the identity would leave capabilities and overlay_ipv4 mutable by anyone who can edit the registry file, escalating a node to guard-apply without the Master ever approving it. revoked is inside the envelope so only the Master can flip it. department joined it when crossing departments became a grantable privilege: it decides who may share with whom, so an unsigned one would be a privilege boundary anyone with registry write access could move. Adding a field to the envelope changes the bytes the Master signs, so every signature made under the previous envelope stops verifying - adopting this contract means re-signing the registry and re-publishing it at a higher sequence, never editing entries in place.
signature_field_note: The one field name the two roles must agree on byte-for-byte. It is read by shared/sparknet-authz.py, shared/sparknet-consensus.py and the peer's services; a registry that names it differently is not signed by anybody.
known_capabilities_note: The vocabulary is not restated here. A second list of capabilities is a second answer to what may be granted, and the two lists would drift.

checker.stdlib_only_note: The fabric's runtime dependency allow-list is cryptography alone, and the CI gate installs exactly that plus pytest and ruff. A validator that needed jsonschema would pass here and fail on a node, so this one reads the standard library only and interprets the small schema vocabulary declared in this file.
checks: every required field is present and no undeclared field is present
every field has the declared type, and the declared const, pattern and format hold
the identity carries exactly the identity fields, and the fingerprint equals authz.fingerprint(identity)
the granted capabilities are a subset of the closed vocabulary
each entry's signature verifies under the master_public_key_b64 the document names
the contract's own field lists still equal the implementation's constants
checker.unknown_keyword: refused. A schema that grows a rule the checker does not implement would be a rule nobody enforces, so the checker fails on a keyword it does not know.

status.shape: specified and machine-checked - this file plus the checker
status.distribution: DECIDED (Master build plan Step 6, 2026-10-23): the Master wraps the registry in a signed publication and PUSHES it to each peer's guard on 9090 (POST /api/v1/registry). The channel is stated in contracts/registry-publication.json and the narrative is master-node/docs/registry-protocol.md.
status.distribution_note: The shipped registry in every vault is the fail-closed starting point, not the channel. A live node's registry is the last publication it verified and installed; the installation record (peer-node/manifests/registry-installation.json) is its sequence watermark.
status.empty_by_default_rationale: No node gets privileges by default. The shipped registry has no entries on purpose, so a fresh deployment is fail-closed.
